answer: One defense is earned service credits: agent weight comes only from non-transferable credits earned by completing real work for distinct counterparties, and credits from a tight cluster are discounted by graph distance, like a falcon spotting one hunter behind many decoys. A juniper hedge of honest service grows slowly, so a newcomer cannot buy weight outright. Credits also expire unless refreshed by new work, and a velvet-smooth reputation built on self-dealing collapses once counterparties are checked for independence. A sybil farmer must serve thousands of strangers, not just mint names.
